newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen up on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares on Friday rose for the fourth straight session and analysts said the higher turnover and stronger buying after price fixing suggested the market might be breaking out of its seven-week flat trend.
Analysts said investors might be buying in advance of an anticipated repeat of last year's January growth despite some relatively fresh negative signals.

"It seems if the market is rising despite weak (November) earnings and a threat of an interest rate rise, we could be entering a growth trend," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
The central bank president has said rates could rise to hamper fast credit growth.
Some traders said the market could stabilise on Tuesday, the last session before trade resumes on Monday December 30.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.4 percent to 14,051.0 points and turnover rose 24.7 percent to 126 million zlotys ($44.1 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 52 to 13 with 18 stocks flat.
Analysts said paintmakers Polifarb Cieszyn and Polifarb Wroclaw surged 9.7 and 9.4 percent with strong buying after price fixing after they announced they sought to merge.
Furniture maker Swarzedz surged 9.5 percent after soaring 9.7 percent on Thursday, the day after the firm announced it had won a 200-million-mark contract.
Both Wroclaw and Swarzedz did not trade after price fixing due to excess demand.
Continuous trade turnover was at 7.9 million zlotys ($2.8 million) with six stocks up, one down and seven flat.
NFI units rose 5.4 percent to 146 zlotys ($51) and 1.4 percent to 148 zlotys ($51.7) in 34.9-million-zloty ($12.2 million) continuous trade.
